skill.name: high-quality-commit
skill.description: Guide AI coding agents through Git commit strategy, including new commits, amend, squash, and interactive rebase decisions.
skill.summary: Create clean Git commits with strategy, message, and verification guidance.
skill.author: AKABANAKK

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown backticks, endpoint examples, and entropy heuristics. Confirmed risk remains because the skill asks agents to stage all files, amend commits, and rebase history. I found no prompt injection, network exfiltration, or obfuscated payload in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Broad staging can include unintended files.
remediation.suggestion: Require git diff and status review before git add -A or any commit operation.

remediation.issue: History rewrite commands can disrupt shared branches.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit approval before amend, rebase, force push, or reset, especially after push.

remediation.issue: Destructive recovery commands lack safety guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Warn that hard reset can discard uncommitted work and recommend backup steps first.

content.value_statement: Messy commit history makes reviews and rollbacks harder. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through commit strategy, messages, and verification.
actual_capabilities: Reviews branch status and commits against main.
Chooses between new commit, amend, squash, and rebase workflows.
Drafts conventional commit messages with subject, body, and footer guidance.
Provides examples for review fixes, WIP cleanup, and staged feature work.
Checks the latest commit and working tree after commit operations.
limitations: It cannot know team Git policy unless the repository documents it.
It may recommend history rewriting that needs user approval.
It does not replace manual review for secrets or unrelated files.
It does not resolve complex rebase conflicts by itself.

use_cases.title: Prepare a feature branch
use_cases.description: Choose between a new commit and an amend before opening a pull request.

use_cases.title: Clean up review changes
use_cases.description: Fold review fixes into an existing commit when they belong to the same logical change.

use_cases.title: Organize complex work
use_cases.description: Plan a small commit series for independent model, API, and UI changes.

prompt_templates.title: Commit current work
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my current Git changes and recommend a safe commit strategy. Ask before running commands that modify history.

prompt_templates.title: Amend review feedback
prompt_templates.prompt: I applied review feedback on this branch. Check whether it should be amended into the previous commit or committed separately.

prompt_templates.title: Split related changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze my staged and unstaged changes. Propose logical commits with clear messages before making any commit.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare branch history
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the branch history against main. Propose an interactive rebase plan, explain risks, and wait for approval before changes.

output_examples.input: I finished a small bug fix and test update.
output_examples.output: Recommended strategy: one new fix commit. The message should describe the validation issue, test coverage, and user impact.

output_examples.input: I made reviewer changes after the first feature commit.
output_examples.output: Recommended strategy: amend the existing feature commit after reviewing the diff. The final message should mention the added validation behavior.

output_examples.input: My branch contains several WIP commits before review.
output_examples.output: Recommended strategy: plan an interactive rebase. Keep logical feature commits, squash small fixes, and ask for approval before rewriting history.

best_practices: Review git status and diff before staging files.
Ask for user approval before amend, rebase, force push, or reset.
Write commit messages that explain why the change was needed.
anti_patterns: Running git add -A without checking for secrets or unrelated files.
Rewriting branch history after others have based work on it.
Mixing unrelated features, fixes, and documentation in one commit.

faq.question: Does this skill create commits automatically?
faq.answer: It provides strategy and command guidance. Agents should request approval before commands that modify history.

faq.question: Can it write commit messages?
faq.answer: Yes. It helps choose a type, subject, body, and footer based on the change.

faq.question: Does it support squash workflows?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends squash or amend when changes belong to the same logical unit.

faq.question: Can it handle interactive rebase plans?
faq.answer: Yes. It can propose a rebase plan for cleaning local branch history.

faq.question: What should I review before using it?
faq.answer: Review changed files, staged content, secrets, and branch sharing status before committing.

faq.question: Is it safe for shared branches?
faq.answer: Use caution. Rebase, amend, reset, and force push require explicit approval on shared branches.
